clue.text: Place quote in speech

indicators.note: in speech means we hear the word spoken rather than see it written, so its spelling may change

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it; said out loud it matches a word for a location

explanation.surface: Someone deciding where to put a quotation within a speech they are writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or spot, such as a building site, so it serves as a noun for a position.

clue.text: Classy dancing pro sure to entertain one

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the jumbled letters hold the numeral
dancing moves around, so the letters of the two words are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A professional dancer, confident of hosting someone elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: Superior can describe something of high quality or someone with refined, upper-class airs, as classy does.

clue.text: Book filled with anger was ultimately boring

indicators.note: something filled with other things contains them, so the volume word wraps the rest

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger

indicators.note: ultimately keeps only the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of was

explanation.surface: A furious book that, in the end, turned out dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was ultimately' reads as 'in the end it was', but 'ultimately' takes just the end of 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and boring both describe something tedious that wears down your interest.

clue.text: Food shop with variety of hams holding appeal for cookery writer

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop for fine foods

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled word grips another piece inside itself
a variety offers different versions, so the following word's letters come in a different order

parts.note: anagram fodder
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A delicatessen offering several hams draws the attention of a food writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is Britain's best-known TV cook and author of cookery books. 'It' for appeal is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith has written many bestselling recipe books, making her a famous British culinary author.

clue.text: Ideal place kept by Tudor monarch south of river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it, so the abbreviation sits inside the royal name

parts.note: Mary I was a Tudor queen
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in addresses

explanation.surface: A perfect spot belonging to a Tudor king or queen, just south of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'south of' puts the monarch below the river. The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary means serving as a perfect model to copy, so it matches ideal as an adjective.

clue.text: Smart, ignoring time, going over lines in happy episode

indicators.note: ignoring the time abbreviation means leaving it out of the word for smart

parts.note: a tidy appearance is a smart, neat one
T is the abbreviation for time
L is short for line, so two make lines

explanation.surface: A clever person, oblivious to the clock, rehearsing their script during a joyful interlude.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'going over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, blissful period or scene, such as a romantic holiday.

clue.text: Term poet changed in fragment, being irritable

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for a small piece

parts.note: a shred is a small torn fragment

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A poet who alters a word in a snippet of verse, being cranky about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short-tempered loses patience quickly and gets angry easily, which is what irritable describes.

clue.text: Certainly popular action

parts.note: something in fashion is popular
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: An affirmation that taking action is sure to win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb used to confirm or emphasise a statement, meaning truly or without doubt.

clue.text: Appendage on alien insect

parts.note: a horn is a bony growth on an animal's head
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A creature from outer space with an extra limb or feeler.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large stinging wasp, one kind of insect.

clue.text: Cut, hard, accepted by lord with variable margin

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the earlier pieces go inside the word for a nobleman

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord
to rip is to tear or cut
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
algebra uses x, y and z as unknown variables

explanation.surface: A noble cuts something, harshly, and has a flexible edge to play with.
explanation.definitionFit: The periphery is the outer edge or boundary of an area, the same idea as a border or fringe.

clue.text: Filled with fear, criticise criminal since apprehending fraud

parts.note: a critic who pans a show criticises it

indicators.note: apprehending means arresting and holding, so the jumbled letters grip the deception
criminal means crooked or bent, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder
a trick is a fraud or con

explanation.surface: Scared after an accusation of wrongdoing, a crook is caught for swindling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for a crook; it is an adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic-stricken describes someone overcome by sudden alarm, utterly terrified.

clue.text: Direct association

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to command someone
second meaning: a society or brotherhood, such as a religious or chivalric body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct association' reads as a phrase about a close link; split it into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To order is to command or instruct, and an order is also a fraternity such as a monastic community.

clue.text: Climbed among debris endlessly

indicators.note: among means the letters sit within the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone has been clambering over rubble that seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like a deletion signal but is just part of the surface; the letters straddle both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past participles of verbs of going upward, so having risen is having ascended or gone up.

clue.text: Plastic money finally, at that point, used in extremity

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the earlier pieces go within the word for an end point

parts.note: a pole is an extremity, such as the North Pole

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of money
then means at that time

explanation.surface: Paying by credit card, the card money running out at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic money' reads as a credit card, but the word 'plastic' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Polythene is a common synthetic polymer used for bags and wrapping, one type of plastic.

clue.text: Commend a fine stirring story by Steinbeck

indicators.note: stirring moves things around, so the letters of the first three words are mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder: all twelve letters

explanation.surface: Someone praising a moving tale written by John Steinbeck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' poses as praise for the story but is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck's 1937 novella follows the migrant workers George and Lennie in Depression-era California.

clue.text: Weed? There'll be awful load in end

indicators.note: awful means terrible or a mess, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener grumbling that in the end there will be a terrible amount of weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: this is one weed among many.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a yellow-flowered plant, a common example of a garden weed.

clue.text: Was ankle injured in ballet?

indicators.note: an injured limb is twisted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a dancer hurt an ankle during a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about Odette, a princess turned into a swan.

clue.text: Prediction from man with tips for company after support

parts.note: a prop holds something up
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: tips are the two ends, so only the outermost letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of company

explanation.surface: A forecast from a man who gives business advice after a backer comes on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After support' places PROP before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophecy is a foretelling of what is to come, so it is a forecast of the future.

clue.text: Doctor in no way tires, resolved to show endurance

indicators.note: in places the medical person inside the rearranged letters
something resolved has been worked out and reorganised, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain

explanation.surface: A physician who never gets tired, determined to demonstrate stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tempts as the anagram signal; here it is GP, and 'resolved' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power is the stamina to keep going over a long period, which is what endurance means.

clue.text: Airman over area spies shrub

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest rank in the RAF
A is the abbreviation for area
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A pilot flying above a region spots a bush below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a verb, sees; it is a noun for an agency. In a down clue, 'over' puts the pieces above.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia, or wattle, is a thorny tree or bush of warm regions, so it qualifies as a shrub.

clue.text: Spoil atmosphere, supporting demon

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting word holds up the one above it, so the atmosphere word goes second, beneath the demon

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A devil propping up a ruined mood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the atmosphere word underneath the demon.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to damage or weaken something, making it worse, which is what spoil means.

clue.text: Board in reach broken by hand with last bit of karate

indicators.note: a word broken by something is split open with that thing inserted in the gap

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it
mitt is slang for a hand

indicators.note: last bit of keeps just the closing letter of the martial art named

parts.note: last letter of karate

explanation.surface: A karate board being smashed by a hand strike, the final move of a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all martial arts, with 'board' as the plank a fighter breaks; it is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A board of directors or governors is a committee, a group appointed to run or oversee something.

clue.text: Complete group turned up, receiving cheers

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the turned word holds the thanks word
in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, so the word comes backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
ta is British slang for thank you, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A whole crowd arriving to applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests applause, but in British usage both cheers and ta mean thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and complete both mean whole or absolute, as in 'a total disaster'.

clue.text: Manage cheerful approach

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
feeling up is feeling happy

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a positive attitude while being in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the approach a bowler or jumper makes before delivery, or the period leading to an event.

clue.text: Work out joke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to solve a puzzle or code
second meaning: a wisecrack or quip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out joke' sounds like getting the punchline, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code is to solve it, and a crack is a witty remark, as in 'a crack about his hat'.

clue.text: Ground that rider regarded as poor

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken down and reassembled

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A horseman judged inadequate by spectators at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' poses as the racecourse or field; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-rate is of low quality, inferior and mediocre, which is what poor means here.

clue.text: Notice concerning new row about a hormone

indicators.note: about means going around, so the pieces before it surround the single letter

parts.note: an ad is a notice advertising something
re means regarding, as in letters
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: An announcement about a fresh quarrel over a gland secretion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument; it is a line. N and LINE together wrap around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands in response to stress, the fight-or-flight chemical.

clue.text: Really essential to deliver yorker

indicators.note: essential to means forming part of the core of the following words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A cricket tip: it is truly vital to bowl a yorker.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery pitched right at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Very and really are both intensifying adverbs, as in 'very good' and 'really good'.
